page: Microsoft Azure D16nlds_v6 is a virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 32 GB of system RAM, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU compute-focused ratio. Additionally, this configuration incorporates 945 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage and support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Belonging to the network-optimized, low-memory branch of the Dnldv6 series, the D16nlds_v6 trades memory volume for a compact resource profile and high local I/O capabilities. While standard general-purpose systems usually feature 4 GB of memory per core, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance here delivers lower per-core memory footprint. This makes it an efficient option for workloads that demand substantial processing power and fast local temporary storage without requiring vast RAM pools. The embedded 945 GB NVMe SSD delivers low-latency scratch space, minimizing external storage dependencies for ephemeral operational data.

Workload applicability centers on compute-intensive and I/O-sensitive applications that operate within moderate memory boundaries. Suitable scenarios include distributed build agents, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, intermediate data transformation, batch compute processing, web serving clusters handling high concurrent traffic, and application tiers requiring fast temporary disk caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D16nlds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs, 32 GB of system memory, and a 945 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, alongside Premium Storage compatibility. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation of 2 GB RAM per vCPU, it operates within the network-optimized and low-memory tier of the Dnldv6 family. Without discrete GPU accelerators, the instance prioritizes dedicated CPU throughput and rapid local NVMe disk access over high memory density. This design yields strong cost efficiency for environments where oversized memory capacities would otherwise lead to idle resource overhead. The server is well suited for batch compute processing, continuous integration pipelines, web application hosting, and intermediate data staging workloads that leverage fast ephemeral local storage.
